title: QBR Facilitator Deck Variants (Standard + Enterprise)
summary: Two facilitator-focused QBR deck templates tailored for Standard and Enterprise accounts. Includes slide-by-slide facilitator notes, pre-meeting prep checklist, a renewal runway tracker, risk scoring matrix, and a compact follow-up playbook. Built to be quick to adapt for different cadence and stakeholder mixes.
body:
Purpose and usage notes:
- Audience: CSMs leading a QBR; AE/solutions + engineering partners invited as needed.
- Variants: Standard (product + adoption focused, 30–45 min) and Enterprise (executive + contractual focus, 60–90 min).
- Intent: Provide a facilitator-first script so newer CSMs can run effective QBRs without heavy slide authoring.

Pre-meeting checklist (to run off 7–10 days before):
- Confirm meeting owners and primary objectives (renewal check, expansion, escalation, alignment).
- Pull topline metrics: ARR, MRR delta since last QBR, active seats, token usage (tokens/day, peak TPS), API error rate (7d and 30d).
- Validate SLAs and incidents since last QBR (SRE summary + any postmortems).
- Customer org update: org chart changes, new projects, key business dates (budget cycles).
- Send pre-read 3 days prior with 2–3 required prep items for customer stakeholders.

Meeting roles and timebox guidance:
- Facilitator (CSM): runs meeting, drives decisions, tracks next steps.
- Technical SME (optional): handles deep technical questions, performance, and SLOs.
- AE / Exec sponsor (Enterprise): drives commercial discussion and renewal/expansion outcomes.
- Timebox: Standard: 30–45 min. Enterprise: 60–90 min with a 10–15 minute exec topline + 30–45 minute detailed review.

Standard variant — Slide-by-slide (30–45 min) with facilitator notes:
1) Title / Objectives (1 slide)
   - Slide: Customer logo, date, meeting objective (e.g., "Renewal health + next 90 days").
   - Note: State desired outcome within first 2 minutes.
2) Quick wins since last QBR (1 slide)
   - Slide: 3–5 bullets (feature launches, latency improvements, cost wins).
   - Note: Praise wins that map to customer goals; call out measurable impact.
3) Usage & health snapshot (2 slides)
   - Slide A: Adoption metrics (active users, integrations, top teams).
   - Slide B: Runtime metrics (avg latency, 95p latency, error rate, token throughput).
   - Note: Keep visuals simple; call out any anomalies and remediation done.
4) Value metrics (1 slide)
   - Slide: Business KPIs tied to Redwood (time to resolution, NLU accuracy, conversion uplifts).
   - Note: If no direct KPI, propose measurement experiment for next quarter.
5) Roadmap / product touches (1 slide)
   - Slide: Upcoming features and dates relevant to the customer.
   - Note: Ask: which features should we prioritize for a pilot?
6) Risks & blockers (1 slide)
   - Slide: Top 3 risks using simple scores (impact x likelihood).
   - Note: Drive decision: accept, mitigate, escalate.
7) Renewal runway & asks (1 slide)
   - Slide: Renewal date, current renewal status, recommended next steps (expand, maintain, caution).
   - Note: For Standard accounts, present 2 action options and preferred next step.
8) Action items & owners (1 slide)
   - Slide: 6–8 line action table (owner, due date, success metric).
   - Note: Confirm owners live; avoid vague commitments.

Enterprise variant — Slide-by-slide (60–90 min) with facilitator notes and exec-ready toplines:
1) Executive one-pager (1 slide)
   - Slide: 3 bullets: business impact, renewal posture (green/amber/red), recommended commercial motion.
   - Note: Exec sponsor opens with 2–3 sentences of alignment.
2) Strategic outcomes & alignment (1 slide)
   - Slide: Map Redwood capabilities to customer strategic goals for next 12 months.
   - Note: Use customer language (revenue retention, product differentiation).
3) Enterprise adoption + integration map (2 slides)
   - Slide A: Org map showing systems using Redwood (product areas, teams).
   - Slide B: Integration status (completed, in-progress, planned).
   - Note: Highlight single points of failure and recommended mitigations.
4) Operational SLOs, incidents & mitigations (2 slides)
   - Slide A: SLO dashboard: latency, availability, error budget consumption (30/90 day).
   - Slide B: Incident digest since last QBR and RCA action status.
   - Note: Bring SRE/Engineering for Q&A.
5) Cost & unit economics (1 slide)
   - Slide: Effective cost per 1k tokens, recommended batching/quantization levers, potential savings scenarios.
   - Note: Tie to finance calendar and renewal negotiation levers.
6) Commercial posture & renewal runway (2 slides)
   - Slide A: Contract overview (end date, auto-renew clauses, current committed capacity).
   - Slide B: Renewal runway: milestones, decision owner, risk level and mitigation plan.
   - Note: Propose commercial motions (price adjustment, committed capacity shift, pilot expansion).
7) Roadmap dependency table (1 slide)
   - Slide: Dependencies between customer deliverables and Redwood deliverables (integration, data feeds).
   - Note: Ask for commitment windows and change control process.
8) Executive decisions & next steps (1 slide)
   - Slide: 3 required decisions to progress renewal or expansion (owner & deadline).
   - Note: Capture decision outcomes in meeting minutes and circulate same day.

Renewal runway tracker (embedded template - use as one-slide appendix):
- Fields: Customer, Renewal date, Current ARR, Forecast ARR at renewal, Last QBR score, Risk score (0-100), Primary decision owner, Next milestone date, Recommended commercial motion, Notes.
- Risk score (example calculation):
   - Usage trend (30% weight): -10 if downward >10% vs last 90d, +10 if >15% growth.
   - SLA incidents (20% weight): -20 if >1 Sev1 in last 90d, -5 per Sev2.
   - Exec engagement (20%): +10 if sponsor engaged monthly, -15 if unreachable.
   - Financial alignment (20%): +10 if renewal in budget window, -15 if out of procurement cycle.
   - Product fit signals (10%): +10 if core use-case, -10 if only experimental.
   - Score normalization to 0-100, cutoffs: >=70 (green), 40-69 (amber), <40 (red).

Risk matrix (2x2 style adapted for renewal):
- X axis: Likelihood (low-high), Y axis: Impact (low-high).
- Quadrants:
   - High Impact / High Likelihood: immediate escalation to AE + Legal + Solution Engineering.
   - High Impact / Low Likelihood: monitoring + contingency plan.
   - Low Impact / High Likelihood: quick tactical mitigations (SLA credits, small pilot).
   - Low / Low: continued monitoring.

Facilitator script fragments (copy/pasteable):
- Opening (30s): "Thanks for joining — objective today is to align on outcomes for the next 90 days and confirm renewal runway. We'll cover toplines, operational health, and ask for two decisions by the end"
- Transition to health: "Quick snapshot — any surprises before I walk through the metrics?"
- Commercial ask (Enterprise): "Given the usage trend and roadmap alignment, we recommend [motion]. What stands in the way of making that decision this quarter?"

Customer-facing pre-read (one-pager template):
- 1-line objective, 3 bullets of recent impact, top 3 metrics, proposed decisions.
- Attach appendix with charts used in the meeting.

Post-meeting playbook (day 0–30):
- Day 0: Send minutes with decisions and RACI.
- Day 3: CSM check-in to confirm next milestone scheduling.
- Day 7–14: Deliverables check (technical tasks, contracts).
- Day 30: Renewal status update and revised risk score.

Lightweight examples and copy snippets (to paste into decks or emails):
- Exec topline: "Over the past quarter, your teams reduced LLM inference cost by 12% while improving 95p latency by 18% — top line outcome is improved conversion from personalized flows."
- Action close request: "Can we lock the decision for X by MM/DD to ensure alignment with your procurement cycle?"

Template caveats & FAQ:
- Keep numerical slides to a maximum of 3 visuals for Standard QBR to respect timebox.
- For technical deep dives, move to a follow-up workshop rather than extending the enterprise QBR beyond 90 minutes.
- If renewal date <60 days, switch to a "renewal sprint" playbook (not included here).

Versioning and local customizations (notes for CSMs):
- Replace all bracketed placeholders before sending to customer (e.g., [ARR], [Renewal date]).
- Use the renewal runway tracker as canonical source of truth in Salesforce/HubSpot — add a link to the tracker in the post-meeting minutes.
- Keep one slide labelled "open issues" for items that require legal or procurement input.

Appendix: sample action item table (copyable)
- Action | Owner | Due date | Measure of success
- Reconfigure batching to reduce cost | Solutions Eng | MM/DD | 8% cost reduction in 30 days
- Confirm exec decision on committed capacity | AE | MM/DD | Signed LOI or verbal commitment

Open questions / to-dos for this template draft:
- Validate scoring weights with Revenue Ops and Product Finance for accurate cost-driven plays.
- Add a short variant that is optimized for mid-market accounts that have >$50k ARR but not full enterprise needs.
- Create a one-slide "FAQ for execs" with contract/term basics to reduce time with legal in early QBRs.

Document history:
- 2025-11-04: initial draft (Priya Shah)
- 2025-12-10: added renewal runway calculator and risk scoring (Liam O'Connor)
- 2026-02-20: updated enterprise roadmap section and cost-savings language (Elena Martinez)

End of document.
